note: Short restatements of what the candidate or their official office published. Empty lists mean no sourced stance was stored. Opponent descriptions are not included. The same issue ids are used for every candidate.

S6KY00286.text: Says bringing down the cost of living, especially fuel prices, is a Senate priority.
S6KY00286.sourceName: Lexington Herald-Leader, Andy Barr written answers

S6KY00286.text: As a House member, voted yes on the Ratepayer Protection Act, which asks states to consider making large data centers pay the added cost of the power they use.
S6KY00286.sourceName: Office of the Clerk, House roll call 312

S6KY00286.text: Says he wants a border wall, more immigration enforcement, and deportation of people he describes as being in the country illegally.
S6KY00286.sourceName: Lexington Herald-Leader, Andy Barr written answers

S6KY00286.text: Says he shares concern about the national debt and that he voted for the 2025 tax and spending law, which he describes as reducing the deficit.
S6KY00286.sourceName: Lexington Herald-Leader, Andy Barr written answers

S6KY00385.text: Says he would rein in tariffs and end cuts to Medicaid that he says raised health costs.
Says he would restore Affordable Care Act subsidies, support a Kentucky public insurance option, and lower prescription prices tied to Medicare negotiations.
S6KY00385.sourceName: Charles Booker campaign, health care policy

S6KY00385.text: Says he supports a national pause on new AI data centers until their effect on water, utility bills, and the environment is known.
S6KY00385.sourceName: Charles Booker campaign, data centers policy

S6KY00377.text: Says health care is a right and that he supports Medicare for All.

H6KY01110.text: His House office says he supports lower taxes, affordable energy, and responsible federal spending.
His House office says he supports protecting rural health providers, strengthening Medicare, and giving patients more control over care decisions.
Voted yes on the Ratepayer Protection Act, which asks states to consider making large data centers pay the added cost of the power they use.
H6KY01110.sourceName: Office of the Clerk, House roll call 312

H6KY01169.text: Says Medicaid should move with a person who relocates, cover free preventive care, and pay providers enough to expand access.
Says he has published proposals on data centers and AI, and names community health, community dividends, and environmental protection as priorities.

H8KY02031.text: Says he works to lower health costs through competition and price transparency, and to expand care in rural communities.
Says companies building data centers, not families and small businesses, should pay for the electricity those centers use.
H8KY02031.sourceName: Official House website, Ratepayer Protection Act statement

H8KY02031.text: Says he voted to fund immigration enforcement and border security through September 2029, and opposes what he calls a return to open borders.
H8KY02031.sourceName: Official House website, Secure America Act statement

H6KY02068.text: Says her first priority is lowering the cost of living, including health care, drugs, housing, and wages, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.
Says she would protect and expand Medicaid, cut paperwork that drops eligible families, and strengthen rural hospitals, mental health, and maternal care.
Says data centers should move forward only with community oversight and public information on energy, water, tax breaks, and local infrastructure.

H2KY03206.text: Says food, gas, utilities, and housing cost too much, and that he would reverse Medicaid cuts he says are raising those costs.
Says he will keep fighting health-coverage cuts and wants people to see a doctor without risking bankruptcy.
Says new data centers should pause until the companies show they will not hurt Kentucky families, and that the community decides what is built nearby.
Says Louisvillians want Washington to stop what he describes as terrorizing immigrant neighbors.

H6KY03223.text: Says families pay too much for housing, energy, and health care, and that she would back more housing, energy supply, tax relief, and fewer regulations.
Says Medicaid should stay in place for people who need it, with stronger checks on fraud and help for people who can work to move into jobs.
Says data centers should pay for the power infrastructure they require, with local input, instead of shifting those costs onto other customers.

H6KY04171.text: Says Medicaid should remain a safety net for children, seniors, and people with disabilities, with eligibility checks and penalties for fraud.
Says a new data center should not add costs for the community, local zoning should decide the site, and utility bills for families should not rise to pay for it.
Says his first priority is fiscal discipline, citing a national debt above $37 trillion, and that he would balance the budget and cut waste.

H6KY04189.text: Says her first priority is lowering costs, including support for small business, manufacturing, and pensions for first responders and teachers.
Says she would move over time toward universal care, restore Affordable Care Act subsidies, add a public option, and protect Medicaid, Medicare, and CHIP.
Says data centers should not be built without community approval, and that the cost should not be passed on to taxpayers.

H0KY05015.text: Says he supports an all-of-the-above energy policy so household electricity costs stay as low as possible.
Says he supports patient-focused changes aimed at more choice and lower costs, and protecting Medicare for seniors and people with disabilities.
Says he voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act so data centers pay for their own electricity and those costs are not added to rural utility bills.
H0KY05015.sourceName: Official House website, data center vote statement

H6KY05152.text: Says he would expand Medicaid eligibility and restore cuts he calls the big ugly bill.
Says he would propose a moratorium on data centers because of concern about collateral impacts.

H6KY05202.text: Says his first priority is shoring up the safety net, including child care, education, food, housing, and utility help, and promoting renewable energy to lower bills.
Says he would undo Medicaid cuts and supports Medicare for All, including vision, dental, and mental health.
Says he supports an indefinite federal moratorium on private AI data centers until Congress regulates AI development.

H2KY05136.text: Says pay should cover the cost of owning a home and raising a family.
Says data centers should not be installed.

H6KY06192.text: At a July 7, 2026 Commerce Lexington forum, said Congress should support an all-of-the-above energy policy so electricity stays affordable as demand from manufacturing and AI data centers grows.
At that forum, said the federal government should not decide where data centers are built, and that local leaders and residents should.

H6KY06184.text: Says he would raise the minimum wage, let Medicare negotiate drug prices, limit corporate purchases of starter homes, and cut child-care costs.
H6KY06184.sourceName: Lexington Herald-Leader, Zach Dembo written answers

H6KY06184.text: Says he would require U.S. drug prices to match prices charged overseas, restore Medicaid, expand Affordable Care Act tax credits, and add a public option.
H6KY06184.sourceName: Lexington Herald-Leader, Zach Dembo written answers

H6KY06184.text: Says Congress should require local hearings before a data center is built and require tech companies to pay their own energy costs.

Says he would secure the border, focus enforcement on people he describes as public-safety threats, fix legal-immigration backlogs, and create a path to citizenship. He says the goal is neither open borders nor mass deportation.
H6KY06184.sourceName: Lexington Herald-Leader, Zach Dembo written answers

H6KY06234.text: Says his first priority is no federal income tax on the first $100,000 of earnings.
Says he supports universal coverage through a public option, nonprofit insurers, or a hybrid, and that private insurance could remain.
Says a community's no on a data center should be final, with no state override.

H6KY06242.text: Says he would seek funding for poor and middle-class families, higher taxes on billionaires, and would not direct that money to AI data centers.
Says he supports Medicare for All and tying U.S. drug prices to prices in other wealthy countries.
Says his first priority is passing the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

H6KY06283.text: Says he would back many small new homes, about 250 to 750 square feet, to add entry-level and senior housing.
Says he would provide a free preventive evaluation so problems are found before later care becomes more expensive.
Says current data centers are too big, employ few local people, and make basic utilities unaffordable.
